title: Inspecting the current directory
description: You can read the directory listing produced by ls -la.

steps.description: You run ls on the current directory. The command supplies the combined options -l and -a.
The -l option requests a long listing with permissions, ownership and size. The -a option includes entries whose names start with a dot.

steps.question: Will this command show the dot entries for the current and parent directories?
steps.answer: Yes. The supplied output includes . and .. because -a includes these entries.

steps.description: You see . and .. as directories and main.sh as a regular file in the recorded listing. This output gives directory contents without printing an absolute path.
